messages:
alice: Heads-up — staging publish blocked by deploy-bot. Deploy bot rejected the manifest list because platform ordering changed (amd64/arm64 swapped) and cosign attestation fingerprint mismatch. Can we triage quickly?

deploy-bot: publish rejected: manifestlist.platform_order_mismatch; cosign: signature_verify_failed (fingerprint diff). See: https://deploybot.internal/rejects/4376543210

ben: ah, that matches a CI change I merged last night — enabled BuildKit inline-cache for cross-arch builds to speed up local caches. It can reorder layers for manifestlist assembly.

carla: quick check: run `skopeo inspect --raw docker://staging.redwood.io/myservice:latest | jq .` and `skopeo inspect --raw docker://staging.redwood.io/myservice@sha256:<digest>` to compare platform array order.

ben: running those now, will paste output in a sec.

ben: output looks like platform array order is swapped compared to the previous manifest we signed. The image contents are identical except for layer ordering metadata.

erin: security note — cosign signature covers manifest bytes, so reorder = signature invalid. We cannot bypass signature verification for prod. Manual attestation is possible but needs KMS sign and approval.

dan: change window is 22:00 PT. If we need to rollback, we should do canary rollback first. Canary at 10% only. We have 45 minutes to decide.

frank: recommendation: rollback canary to pinned digest from last successful deploy, then block further rollouts until we rebuild clean. Manual retag/force-publish is not ideal.

alice: options: 1) rebuild without INLINE_CACHE for the cross-arch job and re-sign (slower), 2) retag previous digest and rollback canary, 3) manual attestation override (needs security + ops). Preferences?

ben: rebuild will take ~18m on CI (multi-arch), but it's the cleanest. I can trigger a rebuild and add a pipeline flag to disable inline cache for multi-arch until we fix manifest assembly.

carla: temporary quick-fix: we can run a lightweight manifestlist reorder tool to canonicalize platform order before signing, but I'm wary of adding a shim. Better to keep build deterministic.

erin: if we do manual attestation, I need a documented justification and an explicit KMS key usage audit entry. Not ideal for a routine publish.

alice: decision: rollback canary to previous pinned digest now, then ben triggers a no-inline-cache rebuild and re-signs. Post-mortem to include CI change notes and a checklist to prevent inline-cache for cross-arch until we have canonical manifest ordering.

dan: executing rollback to sha256:aaaaaaaa... on canary now. I'll monitor metrics and health.

deploy-bot: canary rollback triggered by dan — promoting digest sha256:aaaaaaaa... to canary. Notify when healthy.

frank: keeping an eye on SLOs. If anything degrades, escalate to incident-channel.

ben: started rebuild with `INLINE_CACHE=0 CI_CROSS_ARCH=1 ./ci/build-multiarch.sh --sign`. ETA ~20m. I'll post cosign output here when done.

alice: thanks — I'll update release notes: add entry "publish blocked by buildkit inline-cache causing manifest ordering change; rolled back canary; rebuilding and re-signing." Also adding a change-window hold for the next 24h for cross-arch pushes.

erin: noted. I'll prepare the KMS audit entry template in case we ever need manual attestation.

carla: created an infra ticket to add an assertion in CI: verify manifest platform array stable before signing. Ticket: INFRA-5421

ben: cosign sign complete on new build, signature sha256:bbbbbbbb... running `deploy-bot publish-check` now.

deploy-bot: publish accepted for staging: manifestlist canonicalized, cosign verified.

alice: great. schedule: finish canary ramp after healthy check at +30m, then update release notes + close. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
